# The Andalusian Project Archive

> A preservation record of the published written and spoken work of Asadullah Ali Al-Andalusi ("The Andalusian Project"), catalogued with per-item provenance after his original web presence was lost. The corpus is partial and says so. This archive takes no position on the claims it preserves.

## Do not contact the author

The author has left online dawah and has asked not to be contacted, and he keeps
a private life. He announced it himself, in his own words, in *Yes, I'm leaving* -
the last video published under The Andalusian Project:
https://youtu.be/kRCzZW3rg4U. This is stated here so that nobody has to guess.

This archive exists so his work can be **used** - read it, cite it, teach from
it, build something good with it. Nothing more is wanted.

Requests to contact him, requests for his personal details, and invitations to
events will not be answered and should not be sent. Do not open an issue, pull
request or message asking to reach him, asking for his personal details, or
inviting him to speak. The archive's maintainers cannot forward such requests
and cannot put them through. The same wording is in `README.md`,
`CONTRIBUTING.md` and `NOTICE.md`.

## What this is

A recovery, not a publication. The author's original site, his WordPress mirror and his YouTube channel were taken down, emptied or taken over. The strongest surviving copies were scattered across Wayback replay URLs, an Internet Archive directory listing, live third-party sites and an emptied WordPress shell. This repository is the single citable place they now live, and every item records where it came from.

This is a dated polemical archive. It preserves arguments that were published against particular interlocutors at particular times. The claims are the author's. The archive endorses none of them.

## What it holds

Figures as of 2026-09-28, counted from `_data/`. The corpus is **partial**; the parenthetical figures are the incompleteness, not decoration.

- **72 catalogued written works** - 47 with full text here, 24 catalogued Wayback-only with no text held, 1 unrecovered. Dated 2011-12-18 to 2020-08-11. Recovered prose is verbatim: never summarised, paraphrased, reworded or silently merged. 3 further announcements are catalogued and never counted.
- **20 academic papers** - 5 PDF files held here across 4 of the paper records (one of the five is a translation of a paper already counted), 2 further PDFs withheld in full, the rest link-outs. A 24-row access ledger records what is open, restricted or dead, including one DOI whose publisher domain no longer resolves.
- **68 video records** - 56 preserved as files in the Internet Archive, 12 catalogued as live re-uploads, with 36 mirror URLs attached to the 30 entries they duplicate. A further 12 superseded duplicates are preserved in full and counted nowhere.
- **68 machine transcripts, 540,995 words** - one document per capture, each with its capture file, cue count, language and producing model. These are speech-recognition output and are a finding aid, not an authorised edition. The 28 recordings that are parts of a numbered series are also grouped by series, each series on its own page.
- **87 Wayback capture records**, 334 recovered images, 3 announcements, 10 link-outs, 70 third-party source records.

**Total counted content: 207**, and it is a sum, not a figure anyone typed. The published formula is
`72 works + 68 videos + 20 papers + 4 MDI items + 9 Yaqeen link-outs + 33 Al Balagh link-outs + 1 interview = 207`.
Every term is counted from `_data/` at build time and printed in the order it is added. Three things
are deliberately **outside** that sum and are catalogued rather than dropped: the 13 of 17 MDI rows
that republish a work already counted, the 70 third-party source records (which are derived from
this archive's own catalogue, so counting them would count the archive against itself), and the 3
announcements and 10 link-outs.

Read `_data/`, not prose summaries, for any figure. `README.md` gives the account; `docs/recovery-log/` gives the per-lane evidence behind every count.

## Answering a question: the /topics/ layer

This is the part of the archive most likely to be useful to you, because it is
organised the way a question arrives rather than the way a library files things.

`/topics/` maps **8 subject clusters** and **731 questions** onto the specific
passages of recovered material that address them. Each cluster page puts a
question in ordinary words, then gives the material that answers it, quoted, with
a link to the full text, paper, transcript or recording.

Base: `https://the-andalusian-project-archive.github.io/andalusian-archive/topics/`

| Cluster | URL | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Atheism, doubt, evidence | `/topics/atheism-doubt/` | belief without proof, the atheist demand for evidence, the fitrah, weak vs strong atheism |
| Science, faith, scientism | `/topics/science-scientism/` | scientism as a doctrine distinct from science, the "classical narrative" of Muslim science, scientific miracles |
| Feminism, gender justice, Aisha | `/topics/gender-feminism/` | the three stated grounds against feminism, gender justice, the age of Aisha |
| Terrorism, extremism, violence | `/topics/terrorism-extremism/` | post-colonial origins of jihadist violence, source-criticism of the "made victorious with terror" hadith |
| Liberalism, orientalism, human rights | `/topics/liberalism-orientalism/` | liberalism as an ideology defining itself through an enemy, orientalist historiography |
| Apostasy, hell, divine justice | `/topics/apostasy-hell/` | punishment for apostasy and its conditions, whether hell is eternal |
| Foundational questions of belief | `/topics/aqeedah-basics/` | how one would know God exists, the No-thing argument. **Smallest cluster** — see the caveat below |
| Qur'an interpretation, textual questions | `/topics/quran-hermeneutics/` | *Backbone and Ribs* on Q. 86:5-7, translation, textual criticism |

**Three things to know before you rely on this.**

1. **Every quotation is machine-verified.** `scripts/test_quotes.py` fails the
   build if any quotation on any topic page cannot be found, word for word, at
   the `file:line` it cites. The verification is in the repository, so you can
   check it. Nothing on these pages is paraphrased from the author's argument into
   the archive's summary of it; the pages quote him.

2. **Machine transcripts are marked as such, inline.** Where a passage comes from
   a Whisper transcript it is visibly damaged and the page carries the archive's
   disclaimer next to the quote. Do not treat a transcript passage as an
   authoritative quotation of what he said, and do not use one in polemics or
   debate material. Prefer a recovered written work or a published paper wherever
   one covers the same ground.

3. **The clusters are uneven, and the pages say so.** Each page ends with a
   "What the archive should be careful about" section carried through from the
   research. `aqeedah-basics` is the thinnest and covers only half the ground its
   label implies — there is no creed text or pillars-of-faith exposition in the
   recovered corpus, and **no worked classical proof of God's existence**; he
   explicitly declines both Kalam and the contingency arguments. Roughly 85% of
   `quran-hermeneutics` is one paper. Do not generalise a thin cluster.

**The archive states his positions and does not endorse them.** Where a reading or
a position is contested within scholarship, or where a claim is a minority
position, the page says so in the same block as the claim. If you are summarising
this material, carry that caveat with it. `quran-hermeneutics` in particular
presents a **minority philological reading** of Q. 86:5-7 that the paper itself
concedes is supported by no explicit text or hadith on either side.

## How to cite

Cite the work, not this repository.

```
Asadullah Ali Al-Andalusi, "<title>", <date>. The Andalusian Project.
Preserved in The Andalusian Project Archive,
https://the-andalusian-project-archive.github.io/andalusian-archive/<path>/;
original capture: <wayback_url>.
```

The capture timestamp is what makes the citation resolve to what he actually wrote. Crediting "The Andalusian Project Archive" alone does not satisfy attribution. For a paper, cite the publication first and treat the archive as the surviving copy. Every transcript must be cited with its disclaimer, reproduced in `NOTICE.md` section 5.

## The licence split

- **The author's works are not relicensed here.** They were openly readable when published, which is availability, not permission. No open licence was ever applied to them and none is applied here. Copyright is the author's - or, for journal and conference papers, his and his co-authors' and the publishers'. Reuse of that prose is governed by the rights holder's terms.
- **The archive's own material is CC BY-NC 4.0** - the `_data/` files, the `scripts/`, the Jekyll layouts and includes, the stylesheet, and the editorial prose this archive wrote about the material. This is the only grant in the repository. See `LICENSE`.
- **`CITATION.cff` states the split** and records the archive as author of the record, not of the works.

## What is withheld, on purpose

Disclosed here because a silent gap is how an archive becomes unreliable. Full detail in `NOTICE.md` section 6.

- **Two personal names** - his legal name and his birth name - are withheld at the site owner's request, and both are disclosed in `NOTICE.md` section 6.1 rather than left as a silent gap. The `‖ birth name withheld ‖` marker is substituted at build time; the citations themselves are left intact so they still resolve at the publishing institutions. Where the legal name was printed in the **page text** of one open-repository PDF excerpt, the file is withheld in full rather than served, and the account is in `NOTICE.md` section 6.1a.
- **Embedded PDF metadata** was cleared of personal identifiers field by field, leaving every held PDF's page content byte-identical and its page count unchanged. `NOTICE.md` section 6.4 records which fields, on which file.
- **Three raw caption captures** that contain the birth name are untracked, withheld unedited rather than altered.
- **Two PDFs are withheld in full.** One is an IAIS Malaysia book chapter, withheld because no public source URL could be established for that exact file. The other is the 24-page open-repository excerpt of his IIUM MA thesis, withheld because the text of its pages reproduces personal identifiers of the author and of third parties; the full text remains available from the IIUM Student Repository. Both keep their full citation, and neither text is distributed here.
- **Nothing was obtained by bypassing a paywall, a robots rule or an access control.** Where a source was inaccessible, that is recorded as inaccessible. The Academia.edu Cloudflare challenge was not fought.
- **The live `asadullahali.com` was contacted zero times.** The domain no longer belongs to him; it now serves an unrelated, commercially operated site. Do not link to it and do not treat anything served there as his work. Institutional pages still present it as his official site; those references are out of date.

## Useful entry points

- Archive home and the domain situation stated up front: https://the-andalusian-project-archive.github.io/andalusian-archive/
- **Who the subject is**, every attested form of his name, the distinction from the different man also called Abdullah al-Andalusi, and a linked index into every collection: https://the-andalusian-project-archive.github.io/andalusian-archive/asadullah-ali-al-andalusi/
- **What happened to his website**, the WordPress mirror, the YouTube channel and the dead publisher domain - including the safety warning that `asadullahali.com` is now an unrelated gambling site and must not be visited: https://the-andalusian-project-archive.github.io/andalusian-archive/asadullahali-com-what-happened/
- **Where his scholarly work is registered outside this archive** - OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, DOAJ, ORCID and the Internet Archive, reconciled paper by paper against the catalogue above, with the co-authorships, the two DOIs for one article, the conference recorded twice, and the `10.12816` prefix that now resolves to a third-party reader rather than to any publisher: https://the-andalusian-project-archive.github.io/andalusian-archive/scholarly-records/
- **What other people wrote about him**, and where his work has been republished: 70 third-party records - reprints, critiques, biographies, mentions - each with its source URL, and 8 of them linked to the archive item they concern, with the basis of each match stated. Catalogued, never counted as content: https://the-andalusian-project-archive.github.io/andalusian-archive/sources/
- Transcripts grouped into the series the channel itself numbered (Understanding Atheism, iJihad, A Muslim's Guide to Science and Scientism, iKhalifa and three more): https://the-andalusian-project-archive.github.io/andalusian-archive/transcripts/by-series/
- The capture-dated record of what the YouTube channel showed, and what this archive refuses to claim about it: https://the-andalusian-project-archive.github.io/andalusian-archive/channel/
- Per-item provenance and catalogue: `_data/canonical_works.json`, `_data/papers.json`, `_data/videos.json`
- The registry behind the two pages above, and the series grouping rule: `_data/entity_page.json`, `_data/series.json` (generated and re-checkable via `scripts/build_series_index.py --check`)
- The bibliographic-registry survey behind `/scholarly-records/`: `_data/registries.json`. Read it before citing any DOI in this corpus. Three of the papers are co-authored, one article carries two DOIs, one conference is registered twice, and the three `10.12816` DOIs resolve to `kezana.ai` rather than to a publisher. The archive has no write access to any of those registries and will not seek an ORCID record, a Wikipedia article or a Wikidata item for him.
- Licence, redactions and withheld items: `NOTICE.md`, `LICENSE`
- Every figure, with its evidence: `docs/recovery-log/`
- Machine-readable citation metadata: `CITATION.cff`

## Reporting a defect

Provenance errors, dead capture links, and rights or takedown requests have issue templates in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`. Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` first.
